patch.value: An npm install source that resolved to a local directory is recorded with its bare spec, so freshness checks and upgrades treat it as a registry package

Found in the PR #1782 review (Codex round 5). pm package install npm:plugin installs from disk when plugin is an existing directory relative to the working directory (resolveLocalNpmPackagePath in install-sources.ts), but the managed record keeps only input npm:plugin with location set to the subpath, so nothing records that the install resolved locally. Every later reader re-derives the answer from the spec text: npm-package-arg reads plugin as a registry range, so pm package manage checks the registry for an unrelated published package of that name, the offline update observations (pm-gh1778) can report its version as an update, and pm package upgrade can switch the install to the registry release. Explicit local spellings (./plugin, /abs, file:, tarball paths) are already classified correctly by the shared rule in src/sdk/extension/npm-spec.ts. Fix: persist the resolved source kind (registry or local) on the managed npm source at install time and use it as the single eligibility decision for live checks, observations and upgrade source selection, falling back to the spec rule for records written before the field existed. Duplicate check: searched npm install source local directory registry provenance resolved; pm-u83w (closed) is about absolute paths in the tracked file, not resolution kind.

An npm install that resolves to a local directory records that resolution on the managed source; Live update checks, offline observations and upgrade source selection read the recorded resolution, with the spec rule as the fallback for older records; A test installs npm:<name> from a local directory whose name is also a published package and proves no registry update is reported and upgrade reinstalls the local copy
A locally resolved npm install is never compared with, reported as updatable to, or upgraded to an unrelated registry package
